notes: The first installed version: a desktop shortcut, and updates from inside the app.
Copies camera, sound, stills, drone and 360 cards into a job, onto several drives at once, and checks every copy before a card is marked safe to format.
Several cards at once, one per reader, all copying at the same time.
Jobs come from the drives, or a new one can be made by hand. Folders follow one template, edited in the Folder template tab.
An ASC MHL, a CSV and an HTML report for every card.
A card copied before goes back to its own roll, and a stopped copy can be finished later.
Card readers and drives plugged in by USB, USB-C, SD, CFast or Thunderbolt now always show under Cards and removable drives, even when the reader calls itself a fixed disk.
Each card shows the camera that made it, such as Sony A7S III, when the card says.
A card that was copied and then shot on without formatting only has its new clips copied, into the roll it went to first, and checked. Nothing copied before is touched.
Every section folds, with Collapse all and Expand all.
New scroll bars, and the Roll folder button is now Open folder.
Eject cards and drives from the list, or straight from a card's result after copying.
Cards are named by their camera in the short form crews use (BMPCC 6K Pro), with the card's own name and drive below it (B001 I:\, or Local Disk J:\).
A card that's in the job twice now goes back to the copy filed under the card type you pick, then the first copy made, rather than the latest one.
The fonts are inside the app, so it looks the same with no internet.
The two steps are now Destination and Source.
Eject works: a card in a reader slot is ejected and the reader stays connected, and a reader or drive that Windows treats as a fixed disk is safely removed.
A new job made by Ingest only has a media folder (and its small _htt folder). The rest of a job's folders come from the Heart, so rushes can live on a drive of their own.
The copy panel shows where each copy goes: the card's drive, an arrow, then the destination.
New versions show up straight after they're released.
Roll folders carry the camera's name, such as B001_BMPCC6KPro, A001_SonyA7Siii or S001_ZoomF3.
A card reformatted without changing its reel name no longer stops the copy: if B001 is already used that day, it becomes B001-2. Only the folder; the files keep their own names.
RØDE Wireless PRO cards are recognised by name, and Sony cameras read A7S iii.

A Wireless mics card type: RØDE Wireless, DJI Mic and Hollyland cards get it without asking, and count W001, W002 ... in the Sound folder, so the recorder keeps its own S001, S002 ... whatever order the cards go in.
Ingest remembers the card type you used for each named card (such as F3_SD) and suggests it next time, even when the card doesn't say what made it.
Each card says why its card type was picked, and card types can be set to be picked for a device in the Folder template tab.
A card copied before anything was shot on it, then shot on and copied again, now goes into the same roll. Ingest recognises the card by its serial number, which only changes when it's formatted.
Copying a card with no clips or photos on it gets a note first.
System folders left off a copy are no longer shown on the card; they're still listed in the report.
Insta360 cameras are named, such as Insta360 ONE X2, from their photos or the end of their videos.
RØDE Wireless cards read RØDE however the recorder spells it, so their folders always match.
The Folder template tab now keeps the job folder structure set up in the Heart when it saves its own templates.
A smaller download (about 16 MB again): the build had picked up image and database tools Ingest doesn't use.
New jobs keep their HTT record in pipeline/htt, in step with the Heart's new job layout. Jobs made before keep theirs in _htt, and Ingest finds both.
A studio that never changed its folder template gets the Heart's new layout too. Where cards are copied doesn't change.
The first Heart: it runs on this computer and opens in the browser, with a desktop shortcut and updates from Settings.
Jobs: make a new job, picking where its project folder goes and whether its rushes go on their own drive or inside the project folder. Jobs Ingest made are listed to add, with nothing moved.
Shots: add shots by hand or from a CSV shot list, in sequences in film order, with frame ranges from 1001.
Tasks with statuses, who's on them and due dates, and notes as to-dos you tick off.
A job that's been moved is relinked from its Job settings, and the Heart's own data folder can move to another drive.
Add a job folder: take one existing job folder into the Heart by its job number, such as one made before HTT. Nothing in it is moved or renamed; it gets the job's marker so Ingest sees it's online.

A Structure page: the job folder layout as a tree, each folder folding open or closed, with Collapse all. Pick a folder to change its name (with tokens), when it's made (with every job, or when an app first needs it), what goes there and what it's used for, with an example path. Add, move and remove folders, edit the named pieces, and save it all as the studio default for new jobs.
New versions show up without restarting the Heart: it looks every hour while it runs, and again whenever you open it from its shortcut. A page left open shows the update bar once one is found.

Publish shots from DaVinci Resolve. Add HTT Publish to Resolve from Settings, then in Resolve: Workspace > Scripts > HTT Publish. Colour the VFX clips (Pink to start); clips of that colour become shots, named from the clip if it's already named like a shot, otherwise numbered in tens in the sequence you type.

Resolve renders each shot's plates as EXR at the clip's full resolution, ungraded, with handles, numbered from 1001. Clips stacked under the shot become plates P02, P03. Each shot also gets a review movie and a thumbnail of the edit.

Each version goes into the shot's publish folder (v001, v002 ...) only once it's rendered and checked, so a failed render leaves nothing behind. Speed changes, reframes and short handles in the edit are noted on it.
Shot pages list published versions with Play and Folder, and shot lists show thumbnails.

HTT Publish opens its own publish window instead of a browser tab. It stays on top of Resolve, so you can click around in Resolve behind it; untick Keep on top to let it go behind. Done closes it, and published shots open in the Heart in your browser.

Fixed: HTT Publish stopped inside Resolve just after opening the publish window, so Read the timeline again did nothing and Publish waited forever. Resolve's console works differently from a normal one, and HTT Publish now copes with it.
If HTT Publish stops in Resolve, the publish window says why straight away. A publish Resolve doesn't pick up within a minute is called off, with nothing left behind.
Read the timeline again shows it's reading until the new read arrives.
HTT Publish keeps a log of each run, in HTT's settings folder under resolve.

Plates can go out in ACEScg: HTT Publish converts them through the plate's own timeline colour management, so the project's settings are never touched. ACEScg is the default; Camera space keeps them as shot.
With the grade: plates keep the clip's grade and its colour group's grade, never the timeline's nodes.
Plates go in the shot's plates folder, plates/P01/v003, named ROB_0010_P01_v003, with the review movie and thumbnail in previews/.
Publish only what you want: shots already in the Heart start unticked (All, New only and None to change that), and any shot can be named on the page, such as LAU_0015.
The camera, lens, ISO, shutter, white balance and colour space come from the clip's metadata and show on the shot page, in Frames and Camera sections laid out like the design.
Add version from files: a new version of a plate from an image sequence, such as P01 after paint, copied in and checked. The originals stay as they are.
Tasks can be removed (their notes stay, under General), and are given to people from the crew.
A Crew page for each job: people, roles and access, their open tasks, and adding people, new or from the studio list. You're on every job as its owner.

Previews are always clean Rec.709: the Heart makes each plate's review movie and thumbnail from the plate, through the ACES 2.0 SDR Rec.709 view, so nothing in the Heart is log or raw ACEScg, and your timeline's look (a film emulation) isn't in them. Turn Clean previews off to have Resolve render them from the edit instead.

Plates on projects that aren't colour managed are made your project's way, with your colour group and clip nodes as in the edit, and the Heart converts each frame to ACEScg: from DaVinci Wide Gamut/Intermediate when the grade has a colour space transform, else from the camera's log. The timeline's nodes are never on a plate.
Sony clips are known by their sidecar file: S-Log3/S-Gamut3.Cine goes to ACEScg properly, and the camera and lens show on the shot page.
The camera details on the shot page can be edited: add a lens the metadata didn't have, or change anything.
Put the picked shots in another sequence from the publish window: clips already named like shots kept their own sequence before.
Make the previews again from any version's row.

Plates are smaller by default: compressed EXRs (DWAA, visually lossless and about a third the size) at half the clip's resolution, so a 6K clip makes a 3K plate. Turn either off in the publish window's Settings for lossless PIZ or full resolution.
The publish window has a Settings panel with Colour and Format sections. It folds to one line that says how the plates will come out.
A plate the Heart turns into ACEScg is compressed only once, when it's written, so DWAA's small loss happens once.
Fixed: two preview makers on the same version at once could trip over each other's files.

The publish window shows the previews being made after a publish: a bar for the whole batch, and each plate's frames as they're done, ready, or what went wrong with a Try again button. They carry on in the Heart if you close the window.

Every publish starts with "With the grade" ticked. Untick it for a publish without; it's no longer remembered, so the next publish has the grade again. A clip with no grade goes out from the camera's log as before.

Make a job's DaVinci Resolve project from the Heart: the Resolve project button on the job page, or the tick on New job. It's named after the job, at the job's frame rate and resolution, not colour managed, with a colour group per camera (BRAW, Sony S-Log3 and more) that turns the camera's log into DaVinci Wide Gamut, the bins (rushes, sound, VFX, graphics, music, reference, timelines), HTT's render presets and a first timeline.
Import the rushes too: each shoot day Ingest copied gets a bin, with a bin per camera roll, and the sound goes in the sound bin the same way.
Resolve's cache, proxies and stills go in the job's cache folder instead of on C:, and a copy of the project is saved in the job's edit/resolve folder.
A project of the same name already in Resolve is never touched.
Resolve won't let a script set the playback frame rate, so for a job that isn't 24 fps the job page reminds you to set it in Project Settings. The monitoring format is set to match the job.

Group clips by camera, in the publish window: clips on the timeline with no colour group go into their camera's group (BRAW-DWG, SLog3-DWG and so on), known by their file type or Sony sidecar. A group the project hasn't got is made with HTT's LUT into DaVinci Wide Gamut; one it has is used as it is. Clips already in a group stay where they are.
Plates from clips in HTT's camera groups are converted to ACEScg from DaVinci Wide Gamut, the same as a group with a colour space transform.

An Edit panel on every job page, under the job's name: the job's frame rate, resolution and colour; the Resolve project's settings (project, colour, bins and folders), filled in from the studio's defaults and changeable for that job; making the Resolve project; and the rushes. Every part folds, with Collapse all.
The studio's defaults for the Resolve project are on the Structure page, in its own Edit panel. A job keeps only what it changes, so a default changed later still reaches every other job.

New Resolve projects: grade tools work in DaVinci Wide Gamut (timeline colour space DaVinci WG/Intermediate, with Use Color Space Aware Grading Tools on), output Rec.709 Gamma 2.4, and Scale full frame with crop. Still not colour managed: the camera colour groups do the conversion, as before. Colour management can be switched on in the settings, and then HTT sets Sony clips' input colour space instead of grouping.
New job's resolution list has 6144 x 3456 (was a typo).

Two settings Resolve doesn't let scripts set, the playback frame rate and Use Color Space Aware Grading Tools, are named on the job page when a new project hasn't got them. Ticking the grade tools setting in Resolve's default project settings gives it to every new project.
The job page's Edit panel starts folded, and opened it shows only the Resolve project, first and full width; the settings sub-panels below it stay folded until you need them.
Make it again: a job whose Resolve project was deleted in Resolve can have it made fresh. If the project is still in Resolve, it's left as it is.

The Structure page: every panel folds (Overview, The job folder, Tokens, Named pieces, Edit), with a Collapse all for the page. Tokens and Named pieces sit under The job folder, full width, and Edit under them.

Fixed: making a Resolve project stopped with "not all arguments converted during string formatting" just after Resolve had made it, leaving an empty project. The warning for Use Color Space Aware Grading Tools caused it.
Once Resolve has made the project, nothing stops the rest: a step that goes wrong becomes a warning on the job page, and the project is still saved and copied into the job.

Camera colour groups can use a real Color Space Transform instead of HTT's LUT. The Structure page's Edit panel has a Cameras list: put one Color Space Transform node on a clip in Resolve (the camera's colour space in, DaVinci Wide Gamut out), press Take from Resolve, and the Heart keeps it as that camera's still. New Resolve projects and Group clips by camera put it on the group's pre-clip node. A camera without a still keeps HTT's LUT.
Stills can be loaded from a .drx file too, and HTT's own ship inside the installer, so every install has them. Replaced stills are kept, never overwritten.

Camera colour groups now convert with a DCTL instead of a LUT: the same maths as a Color Space Transform from the camera's log into DaVinci Wide Gamut / Intermediate (tone and gamut mapping none), read from OpenColorIO's config. It doesn't clip above 1.0 the way the LUT could, and a Sony plate through it matched a straight conversion to within 0.002%.
When HTT brings a newer OpenColorIO, the DCTLs are made again from it, so its corrections reach every camera. The Cameras list on the Structure page shows which are up to date.
BRAW, Sony (S-Gamut3, S-Gamut3.Cine and Venice), ARRI LogC3 and LogC4, RED, Canon Log 2 and 3, Panasonic V-Log, DJI D-Log and Apple Log are all ready.
Take from Resolve and Load a .drx are gone: Resolve's scripting can't put a still on a colour group.

Camera Pre Groups: pick which cameras a new Resolve project gets a colour group for. The studio default on the Structure page has every camera; a job's Edit panel can cut it down to the two or three it uses.

The main cameras are all there: Blackmagic Gen 5, Sony S-Log3 (S-Gamut3.Cine, S-Gamut3, Venice), ARRI LogC3 and LogC4, RED Log3G10, Canon Log 2 and 3, Panasonic V-Log, Apple Log and DJI D-Log. ARRIRAW (.ari LogC3, .arx LogC4), RED .r3d and Canon .crm clips are put in their groups by Group clips by camera, as BRAW and Sony already were.
Groups are named BMDgen5-DWG, slog3 and so on, and each DCTL is named after its group, so the node reads LUT: BMDgen5-DWG.
Always a DCTL: there's no LUT fallback any more.
Bug fixes from a full check of the code.
Publishing: if the Heart can't record one plate, the others still publish, and the page says where that plate's frames are. Before, one failure showed every plate as failed.
Publishing: moving picked shots into a sequence never gives one the number of another picked shot already in it.
Cinema DNG and Nikon N-RAW clips are treated as RAW (Resolve decodes them), so they're no longer flagged as having an unknown colour space.
A job's frame rate and resolution are checked when they're changed, so a typo can't stop its Resolve project being made. A task's due date is checked the same way.
Going back a version in Updates no longer risks tidying away the installer it's about to run.
Previews: one queued just as the Heart finished the last one could wait forever. Previews also hold only a few frames in memory at a time.
Structure page: the Camera DCTLs list folds on its own, apart from Camera Pre Groups.

Node names: Resolve doesn't let scripts name a node (its scripting can read a node's label but not set one), so the camera groups' nodes show no name. The group's name is on the colour group itself, and its DCTL file is named after it.

A new job layout, from the planning doc: a pipeline folder for HTT's own files, Blender's project file, and each shot's work split into 2d and 3d, then the task, then a folder per piece of work (3d/lighting/ROB_0010_lighting, 3d/fx/ROB_0010_fx_tank) with the app's own folders inside.

Everything published goes in one publish folder laid out like the shots, plates included. Like the rushes, it can be on its own drive per job, such as a fast drive for renders and plates: pick it when making a job, or in Job settings.
Each job gets a Blender project file (Blender 5.3): every .blend in the job uses the same ACES 2.0 colour as the Heart, and the job's published assets show in Blender's asset browser.

The start of Pulse, as a page in the Heart: pick a shot's task and open it in Blender (any version installed). The first time, its folders are made and the scene is set up from the shot: frames from 1001, fps, resolution, ACEScg, the plate behind the camera, renders as EXR. After that the latest version opens.

HTT for Blender, in the 3D View's sidebar: Save new version, Test render (kept in the work folder), and Render for comp, which renders straight into the publish folder and is recorded by the Heart, with its review movie, so comp sees it at once.
Review movies are made from multilayer EXR renders too.
Studios that never changed the folder list get the new layout. Jobs made before keep their folders and their _htt record.

Fixes 0.10.0 not opening on a Heart that already has jobs ("FOREIGN KEY constraint failed"): its database update now adds the publish root without rebuilding the jobs table. Nothing was lost: the failed update had changed nothing.
